subject.name: Manarat Foundation
subject.positioning: First purpose-established masjid and Islamic centre for the Muslims of Sheldon, Solihull and surrounding areas; founded by a group of scholars; explicitly promotes tolerance and rejects extremism
services: Five daily prayers and Jumu'ah congregations
Quran recitation, Tajweed and Islamic studies
Three-year Hifz ul-Qur'an programme (weekday and weekend)
Arabic language course for children
Character development
Nikah - Islamic and civil marriage registration
Local charitable and social welfare work

website.prayer_times: PDF only, uploaded 2020-07 (/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Manarat-Foundation-Prayer-Timetable-3.pdf); no live on-site timetable

competitors.name: Jami Mosque & Islamic Centre Birmingham (JMIC)

competitors.address: 521-527 Coventry Road, Small Heath, Birmingham B10 0LL

Hifz madrasa (since 1983)

Raheem Academy - evening and weekend maktab, ages 5-16
Muslim funeral services (since 1995)
Social welfare
JMIC Muslimah - dedicated women's programme
Community services

website.depth: Deep - structured service tree with individual sub-pages
website.campaign_example: Ramadan Appeal 2026 - dedicated donation form page

competitors.key_lesson: Only 19% of income comes from donations. Rental property and education fees carry the organisation, which insulates it from donation-cycle volatility.

competitors.name: Solihull Islamic Education Academy Ltd (SIEA)
competitors.why_a_competitor: Not a masjid, so it does not compete for prayer footfall - but it competes directly for the same Solihull families' children and their weekend education spend, which is Manarat's core programme.
services: Solihull supplementary Sunday school
Mother-tongue language teaching - Arabic, Bangla, Urdu
Weekly adult Islamic education
Talks on Islam in schools and community organisations
Weekly badminton and football youth clubs for teenagers
competitors.key_lesson: Mother-tongue languages beyond Arabic (Bangla, Urdu) and sport-based youth clubs reach families that a prayer-and-Quran-only offer does not.

competitors.name: Solihull Central Masjid & Community Centre
competitors.why_a_competitor: The nearest masjid inside Solihull proper. Manarat's claim to be 'the masjid for Sheldon and Solihull' weakens as this site matures.

financials.note: Nil return filed; published figures do not reflect actual activity. Reporting is up to date.

services: Daily prayers, Jummah, Eid (twice yearly) and Taraweeh
Qur'anic studies, Islamic education and Arabic language classes
Lifelong learning and personal development programmes
Marriage services and family support
Interfaith meetings, community gatherings, talks and workshops
positioning_angles: Catering equipment hire - an unusual earned-income line
competitors.key_lesson: Competes on convenience (town centre, motorways, parking) rather than scholarship, and monetises the building through catering equipment hire.

competitors.name: Deen Central
competitors.why_a_competitor: Overlapping Solihull catchment and a similar education-plus-community pitch, but currently financially distressed.

financials.note: No published charity figures located. The organisation has publicly stated that its donor income dropped by almost 100% while daily masjid overheads continued.

competitors.positioning: A safe, open space for Islamic education, community and spiritual nurturing
competitors.key_lesson: A live cautionary case: a single-source donation model with fixed building overheads is fragile. Also a potential partnership or absorption opportunity rather than a pure rival.

Educational college

Welfare services

website.recurring_offer: Consistent Deeds - £20/month, framed as 67p a day

competitors.key_lesson: Every giving ask is a named project with a page of its own, and the flagship ask is recurring monthly giving priced as a daily habit. 94% of income is deployed, which is itself the fundraising argument.

feature_matrix.legend: true = present, false = absent, string = qualifier

findings.title: No native online donation flow
findings.detail: Manarat's published donation routes are cheque and in-person giving. Every tier-1 competitor except SIEA takes card payments on or from its own site, and online giving is intermediated for Manarat by MosquePay. Cheque-and-cash giving structurally excludes under-40 donors and makes Ramadan night-giving - the single highest-intent moment in the Islamic giving calendar - almost impossible to capture.
findings.evidence: Manarat donation page lists cheque and in-person only; JMIC runs /donate/ plus campaign forms; GLMCC and Solihull Central both take online payments.

findings.title: Prayer times are a six-year-old PDF
findings.detail: The timetable on the site is a PDF uploaded in July 2020. Prayer times are the highest-frequency reason a local Muslim opens a masjid website, and that recurring traffic is currently being handed to MosquePay, The Masjid App and MosqueFinder. JMIC, Deen Central and GLMCC all host live timetables themselves.
findings.evidence: /wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Manarat-Foundation-Prayer-Timetable-3.pdf; a Manarat timetable is also hosted on mosquefinder.co.uk.

findings.title: Only 61% of income is being spent
findings.detail: Income of £394,135 against expenditure of £239,198 leaves a surplus of roughly £156k in a single year. GLMCC deploys 94% of income and SIEA 86%. Either Manarat is quietly building toward a capital project - in which case that project is not named anywhere public and is therefore not raising money - or it is under-deploying. Both readings point to the same fix: name the project.

findings.title: Single-source income concentration
findings.detail: Manarat appears to be almost entirely donation-funded. JMIC takes only 19% of its income from donations, carrying the rest on rental property and education fees; Solihull Central hires out catering equipment; SIEA charges course fees. Deen Central, which is donation-only, has publicly reported a near-total collapse in donor income while overheads continued. Manarat has a 1,000-capacity building with a large car park and no visible earned-income line.
findings.evidence: JMIC FYE 2024 breakdown; Deen Central public statement.

findings.title: Thin site with no per-service pages
findings.detail: Roughly five top-level pages against JMIC's service tree and GLMCC's project-per-page structure. Manarat's Hifz programme, Arabic course and combined Islamic-plus-civil marriage registration are each strong enough to justify their own page, and each is a distinct search entry point currently collapsed into one /services/ page.
findings.evidence: Known page lists for each domain.

findings.title: No funeral or janazah service
findings.detail: JMIC has run funeral services since 1995 and GLMCC offers them. A bereaved family that has to go to Small Heath at the hardest moment of their lives tends to keep going there afterwards. This is the highest-loyalty service in the sector and Manarat does not appear to offer it.
findings.evidence: JMIC funeral services since 1995; no equivalent found for Manarat.

findings.title: No visible women's or youth programme
findings.detail: JMIC runs JMIC Muslimah with its own site section; SIEA runs weekly badminton and football youth clubs; GLMCC runs extensive outreach. Manarat's public offer is prayers, Quran, Arabic and Nikah, which reaches men and children but not women or teenagers as distinct constituencies.

findings.title: Discoverability is rented, not owned
findings.detail: Manarat is listed on MosquePay, The Masjid App, MosqueFinder and Giving is Great. Those aggregators own the donor relationship and the recurring visit. They are useful acquisition channels but should not be the primary one.

findings.title: The strongest differentiator is unstated
findings.detail: Manarat was founded by a group of scholars, is the first purpose-established masjid for Sheldon and Solihull, and explicitly promotes tolerance and rejects extremism. That last position is rare, publicly valuable and completely absent from how the site sells itself. Solihull Central competes on parking and motorway access; Manarat can compete on scholarship and civic trust.
findings.evidence: Manarat about-us content; Solihull Central positioning.

recommendations.action: Put a live prayer timetable on the site, auto-calculated and mobile-first, with Jumu'ah and Janazah announcements
recommendations.rationale: Recovers the highest-frequency reason to visit, and every other ask can then be placed next to it.

recommendations.action: Add a native online donation flow with card and Apple/Google Pay, plus Gift Aid capture
recommendations.rationale: Gift Aid alone is worth 25p per eligible pound and is currently uncollected on cash and cheque giving.

recommendations.action: Name and publish the capital project the £156k surplus is building toward, as a dedicated appeal page with a progress figure
recommendations.rationale: GLMCC's model: an unnamed reserve raises nothing, a named project raises money and explains the surplus at the same time.

recommendations.action: Launch a recurring monthly giving tier priced as a daily habit, mirroring Consistent Deeds
recommendations.rationale: Converts volatile seasonal giving into a predictable base. 200 donors at £15/month is £36k of certainty.

recommendations.action: Split /services/ into a page per programme - Hifz, Arabic, Islamic studies, Nikah - each with fees, times, age range and an enquiry form
recommendations.rationale: Four search entry points instead of one, and it removes the phone call currently required to learn basic details.

recommendations.action: Introduce a funeral and janazah service
recommendations.rationale: The single highest-loyalty service in the sector and the clearest reason Sheldon families currently travel to Small Heath.

recommendations.action: Open a second income line from the existing building - hall hire, the car park, or paid short courses
recommendations.rationale: A 1,000-capacity building with a large car park is an under-used asset; Deen Central shows the cost of donation-only funding.

recommendations.action: Start a women's programme and a youth activity, each with its own page
recommendations.rationale: Matches JMIC Muslimah and SIEA's sport clubs, and reaches the two constituencies the current offer misses.

recommendations.action: Lead the homepage with scholarship, the Sheldon-Solihull first-mover story, and the anti-extremism position
recommendations.rationale: The one thing no local competitor can copy.
